question.value: Uncover the location, morphology, and extinction of obscuring dust filaments in the central kpc of nearest type 1 and intermediate-type AGN, and their relation to nuclear ionised and molecular gas.

evidence.quote: This paper examines their existence in an equivalent sample of the nearest type 1 and intermediate-type AGN and evaluates the obscuration they may introduced on these unobscured nuclei.

The aim of this work is to uncover the location and morphology of obscuring material in the central kpc of the galaxies sample, and its distribution and location with respect to that of central ionised gas, and of the nucleus.

findings_qualitative.value: Long, narrow dust filaments and lanes (extending hundreds of pc to kpc) are ubiquitous in the central parsecs of type 1–1.9 AGN, with M87 as the sole dust-free exception.

evidence.loc: Nuclear dust: morphology, location, and extinction
evidence.quote: The dust maps (Section [2.3](#sec:DustMaps_extinction)) show the ubiquity presence of obscuring material in the central parsecs of all the study galaxies, the sole exception is M87.

findings_qualitative.value: In type 1–1.9 AGN, optical and IR nuclear peaks coincide within astrometric precision (10-40 mas), whereas in type 2 AGN they are shifted by a few parsecs due to optically thick crossing filaments.

evidence.loc: Nuclear dust: morphology, location, and extinction
evidence.quote: Yet, in the present sample the optical and IR peak, amid the filaments and lanes crossing the centre, always coincide in position, within our precision astrometry of few tens of mas, i.e. parsec to sub-parsec scales (Table [\[tab:extinction\]](#tab:extinction)).

findings_qualitative.value: Because the dust extinction in type 1–1.9 filaments is moderate (typically A_V < 2 mag), nuclear ionised gas overlaps and interlaces with dust structures rather than showing the strict spatial anti-correlation seen in type 2 AGN.

evidence.quote: On the contrary, in the present sample, the ionised gas spreads all over the nuclear region in most cases regardless of the dust location. This overlap may be due to two reasons: 1) the low extinction of the filaments and lanes, typically $A_V < 2\, \rm{mag}$

findings_qualitative.value: Nuclear dust filaments have direct counterparts in molecular gas (e.g. ALMA CO(3-2) in NGC 1566), acting as streamers channeling material from galactic scales into the nucleus.

evidence.quote: Filaments and lanes are traced by equivalent structures in molecular cold and warm gas in CO, HCN and $H_2$. A single filament can be seen either getting straight- or spiralling- to the centre, suggesting their role as streamers to channel material from galactic scales to the centre.

claims.hypothesis: Large-scale host galaxy dust filaments and lanes found crossing the nuclei of type 2 AGN are also ubiquitous in the central parsecs of type 1 and intermediate-type AGN, but with different location or lower optical depth.
claims.experiment: Constructed high-resolution (<200 mas) near-IR (VLT/NaCo) to optical/UV (HST) colour and extinction maps of 9 nearby type 1–1.9 AGN registered to 10-40 mas precision.
claims.result: Dust filaments and lanes are found in the central parsecs of 8 out of 9 galaxies (except M87), located next to the nucleus or crossing it with low extinction (A_V typically <= 1.5 - 2 mag, factor 2-3 lower than in type 2 AGN), and optical/UV peaks coincide with 2 um peaks.
claims.finding: Large-scale dust filaments are a common ingredient in galaxy centres and can naturally produce the type 1/2 AGN dichotomy depending on whether they cross the line of sight and their optical depth gradient, playing the role of the torus.

evidence.quote: The same type of narrow, collimated, dust filaments are equally found at the centre of these AGN. The difference now resides in their location with respect to the nucleus, next to it but not crossing it, as it is the case in type 2, and their reduced optical thickness towards the centre, $A_V \lesssim 1.5\, \rm{mag}$

Their location with respect to the nucleus and increasing gradient in optical depth towards the centre could naturally lead to the canonical type 1 / 2 AGN classification, making these filaments to play the role of the torus.

claims.hypothesis: The spatial distribution of nuclear extended ionised gas in AGN is shaped by the optical thickness and location of nuclear dust filaments rather than a parsec-scale torus.
claims.experiment: Extracted continuum-subtracted HST [OIII] and H-alpha+[NII] emission maps registered to mas accuracy and overlaid them on the IR/optical dust maps.
claims.result: In most type 1–1.9 AGN where A_V < 2 mag, ionised gas and dust overlap symmetrically around the nucleus; spatial anti-correlation only appears where filaments have higher extinction (A_V ~ 2-3 mag, as in NGC 1365).
claims.finding: Low filament optical depth in type 1–1.9 AGN is insufficient to suppress extended ionised gas, explaining why gas and dust interlace and why ionised gas collimation is less frequent in type 1 than in type 2 AGN.

evidence.loc: Nuclear ionised gas location relative to the dust
evidence.quote: Only in those galaxies with the highest extinction towards the centre, $A_V \sim 2$–$3\, \rm{mag}$, an spatial anti-correlation between the dust and the ionised gas is observed.

evidence.loc: Nuclear ionised gas location relative to the dust
evidence.quote: In the current type 1 -1.9 sample, the filaments optical thickness is insufficient to suppress the extended ionised gas in most cases, hence gas and dust interlace in the centre, and no collimation or preferential direction in the ionised gas is seen

claims.hypothesis: Nuclear dust filaments trace molecular gas streamers that channel mass inflows to feed the AGN.
claims.experiment: Compared the nuclear dust extinction map of NGC 1566 with archival high-resolution ALMA CO(3-2) cubes and kinematic maps to isolate a 150 pc spiralling filament and compute the mass inflow rate.
claims.result: The dust filaments match CO(3-2) molecular gas structures in blueshifted channels (20-80 km/s), yielding an estimated mass inflow rate of <~ 0.16 - 0.2 M_sun yr^-1.
claims.finding: Dust filaments trace molecular gas inflow channels whose mass inflow rates (<~ 1 M_sun yr^-1) are orders of magnitude larger than the Eddington accretion rates needed to sustain low-Eddington AGN activity.

evidence.loc: Dust filaments traced by molecular gas: streaming material to the centre
evidence.quote: The estimated inflow rate, $\sim < 0.2\, \rm{M_\odot\,yr^{-1}}$ is more than enough to support the mild activity of this nucleus, with an Eddington accretion rate two order of magnitude lower.
Dust filaments and lanes show equivalent morphologies in molecular gas. Available gas kinematic indicates mass inflows at rates $< ~ 1 M\odot~ yr^{-1}$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Compact parsec-scale donut-like dusty torus as the universal cause of AGN 1/2 dichotomy and NLR ionised gas collimation is challenged in favour of hundred-pc to kpc scale host-galaxy dust filaments and lanes.

evidence.quote: Their location with respect to the nucleus and increasing gradient in optical depth towards the centre could naturally lead to the canonical type 1 / 2 AGN classification, making these filaments to play the role of the torus.

evidence.quote: Thus, it was concluded that the typical nuclear ionisation cones and collimated morphologies that characterise the narrow line region in the sample are not caused by a parsec-scale collimating torus as envisaged by the AGN unified model but simply by the location / morphology of the filaments and lanes in the central region ((cite: Prieto2014)).

limitations_admitted.value: Reported A_V values cannot measure extinction at the nucleus itself, only in its surroundings (tens of pc away), because nuclear colours are contaminated by AGN non-thermal emission and hot dust emission.

evidence.loc: Dust maps and extinction in the central kpc
evidence.quote: Also we note that the reported $A_{\rm{V}}$ values do not measure any extinction at the nucleus itself but at its surrounding, typically within ten of parsec from the centre: nuclear colors are not representative of extinction as both non-thermal emission and presumably dust in emission from the AGN also contribute to these colors.

limitations_admitted.value: In star-forming regions, jets, or the steep UV nuclear continuum where optical emission is intrinsically stronger than IR, the colour maps do not measure dust extinction.

evidence.loc: Dust maps and extinction in the central kpc
evidence.quote: At these locations, included the nucleus as just discussed above, the maps do not measure dust extinction but simply the stellar or non-thermal contribution.

limitations_admitted.value: For NGC 3081 and NGC 3783, no point-like clusters other than the nucleus were available in the FoV, so image registration had to rely on the nucleus itself.

evidence.quote: By default the nucleus is not used in the alignment process, with the exceptions of NGC 3081 and NGC 3783 (Table [\[tab:general_info\]](#tab:general_info)) with no point-like sources other than the nucleus in the field of view. In these cases the registration relies on the nucleus only.

referee_caveats_inferred: Because NGC 3081 and NGC 3783 were registered using the nucleus itself, the conclusion that optical and IR nuclear peaks coincide cannot be independently tested in those two galaxies.

The mass inflow rate estimate in NGC 1566 relies on strong geometric and physical assumptions (filament depth equal to width, volume filling factor of 1, dust-to-gas ratio from Milky Way) and an inflow velocity read off a literature CO(2-1) map rather than fitted directly to the CO(3-2) cube.
Extinction values A_V are measured 0.5'' to 1.5'' (tens to hundreds of pc) away from the AGN, so extrapolating their optical depth to sub-parsec nuclear scales to replace the torus remains indirect.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~5-20 GB (one archival ALMA Band 7 spectral cube for NGC 1566 plus HST WFPC2/ACS and VLT/NaCo 2D images for 9 galaxies)
reproducibility.score_reason: Raw VLT, HST, and ALMA data are in public archives and the ALMA analysis uses standard pipeline cubes, but exact aperture coordinates for A_V measurements, continuum scaling factors, and the specific extinction law conversion formula are not explicitly provided in the text (referred to earlier papers).
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: ALMA data play a minor supporting role for a single galaxy (NGC 1566), where the main numerical result (inflow rate) is an order-of-magnitude back-of-the-envelope calculation combining visual extinction, assumed geometry, and a velocity taken from literature.
